thread:
lina: quick heads-up — canary showed inconsistent read when we did a soft-evict/handoff. small repro below
raj: logs?
lina: paste:
```
HANDOFF start prefix=acct-900 epoch=210
REQ id=0xdead enter fastpath -> pin ok (epoch=210)
LEASE revoke prefix=acct-900 epoch=211
HANDOFF commit -> owner=shard-9
REQ id=0xdead finalize -> served by old owner
```
alex: so we allowed the read to proceed after the pin check but before the lease/handoff finished. that's the gap.
sophia: tradeoff was p99. we avoided blocking finalization to keep latency low. still, correctness matters.
raj: proposal: add epoch-fence recheck at response-commit. If the request's observed epoch < current epoch && handoff flag active, return RETRY_HANDOFF.
lina: runtime returns a typed error; gateway does a single transparent re-route to owner-resolve & forward. no client-visible retries beyond one.
alex: restrict to read-only ops (GET/SCAN/LOOKUP). writes must still be serialized/stalled.
sophia: feature-flag this (evict.epoch_fence_retry=false by default). metric: `prefix.handoff_retries.count` and dashboard. ops-bot can hook alerting.
ops-bot: metric placeholder created. suggested alert: >8/min sustained on canary pool.
raj: tests: unit for epoch flip, integration harness to inject revoke during in-flight read, then canary rollout.
lina: long-term option: brief quiesce (50-200ms) at exact swap point to make handoff atomic. prefer as follow-up after metrics.
alex: decision for now: implement cheap epoch-fence + RETRY_HANDOFF for read-only, gateway single re-route, behind feature flag. I'll open runtime + gateway PRs. lina will own canary and metrics.
lina: thanks, will file tickets & link PRs. :thumbsup:
